items.title: Socialist defeats far-right rival in Portugal presidential runoff

featured_image.name: Portugal chooses between a moderate and a populist in runoff presidential election

items.description:
António José Seguro, the center-left Socialist candidate, scored a decisive victory over far-right populist André Ventura in Portugal's presidential runoff election on Sunday, according to exit polls conducted for the nation's three major broadcasters. The moderate Seguro secured approximately 67 to 73 percent of the vote, while Ventura received between 27 and 33 percent.[1][2][3]

The result marks a resounding defeat for Ventura's anti-establishment Chega party, which had become Portugal's second-largest parliamentary force after winning 60 seats in the May 2025 general elections. The runoff was the first presidential election in Portugal to require a second round in 40 years, since the 1986 contest.[4][5][6][7][8][9]

items.title: Iran sentences Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi to 7 more years

featured_image.name: Iranian Nobel Peace Laureate Starts New Hunger Strike in Prison

items.description:
Iran has sentenced imprisoned Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi to more than seven additional years behind bars after she began a hunger strike, delivering the verdict as Tehran negotiates with the United States over its nuclear program.

Her lawyer, Mostafa Nili, confirmed the sentence on X on Sunday, saying a Revolutionary Court in the city of Mashhad handed down the ruling on Saturday. Mohammadi received six years for "gathering and collusion to commit crimes," one and a half years for propaganda activities, a two-year travel ban, and two years of internal exile to the city of Khosf in South Khorasan province. Under Iranian law, prison sentences run concurrently, meaning the longest term applies.[1][2][3][4]

Iranian authorities have not publicly acknowledged the ruling.[2][5]

items.title: Starmer's chief of staff quits over Mandelson appointment

featured_image.name: Morgan McSweeney quits: Keir Starmer's right-hand man ...

items.description:
Morgan McSweeney, the architect of Labour's 2024 general election victory, resigned as UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer's chief of staff on Sunday, taking responsibility for advising the embattled leader to appoint Peter Mandelson as ambassador to the United States.

"The decision to appoint Peter Mandelson was wrong. He has damaged our party, our country and trust in politics itself," McSweeney wrote in his resignation letter. "When asked, I advised the Prime Minister to make that appointment and I take full responsibility for that advice. In public life responsibility must be owned when it matters most, not just when it is most convenient."[1][2]

The resignation marks a dramatic fall for the Irish-born strategist who masterminded Starmer's transformation of the Labour Party and its landslide victory in July 2024. McSweeney had been considered indispensable to Starmer's political operation, with one minister previously telling reporters the pair were "locked together in mutual survival."[3][4]

items.title: Japan's Takaichi wins landslide in snap election, exit polls show

featured_image.name: Japan's Leader Wins in a Landslide, Clearing Way for Hard-Line ...

items.description:
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's gamble on a snap election has paid off handsomely. Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party swept to a commanding victory on Sunday, with projections from public broadcaster NHK showing the party capturing at least 310 seats in the 465-member lower house—far exceeding the 233 needed for a majority and marking a dramatic reversal from the party's fortunes just months ago.[1][2][3]

Together with coalition partner Japan Innovation Party, Takaichi's ruling bloc is projected to win between 302 and 366 seats, potentially securing a two-thirds supermajority that would allow the government to override vetoes from the opposition-controlled upper house.[4][5][2]

items.title: Chang'e-6 samples confirm uniform impact rates across Moon

featured_image.name: China's Chang'e-6 collects first rock samples from Moon's ...

items.description:
Chinese scientists have confirmed for the first time that impact cratering rates on the Moon's near and far sides are essentially consistent, paving the way for a unified global lunar chronology system. Separately, researchers using Chang'e-6 samples have found evidence that a giant ancient impact reshaped the Moon's interior, potentially explaining why Earth's only natural satellite looks so different on its two hemispheres.

The findings, published in Science Advances on Thursday and in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in January, mark breakthroughs in understanding the Moon's 4.5-billion-year history, drawing on the first samples ever returned from the lunar far side.[1][2][3]

items.title: India, Malaysia sign 11 agreements on trade and semiconductors

featured_image.name: India, Malaysia renew pledges to boost trade, collaboration - Reuters

items.description:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim signed 11 cooperation agreements on Saturday as the two nations seek to deepen ties in semiconductors, trade, and defense following discussions in Putrajaya.

The signing ceremony, which took place at Anwar's official residence in Malaysia's administrative capital, marked what officials described as one of the most comprehensive upgrades in bilateral relations in recent years.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump to host Board of Peace summit on Feb. 19 in Washington

featured_image.name: Trump to hold first Board of Peace meeting this month in Washington

items.description:
Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban announced Saturday that he will travel to Washington in two weeks to meet with President Donald Trump at the inaugural meeting of the Board of Peace, set for February 19. The gathering will focus on advancing the Gaza ceasefire and raising funds for the territory's reconstruction.

"I got an invitation: two weeks from now we will meet again with the US president in Washington, because the Board of Peace, the peace body, will have an inaugural meeting," Orban said at a campaign event, according to The Times of Israel.[1]

items.title: Chinese scientists turn CO2 into petrol components using solar power

featured_image.name: How Chinese scientists made petrol building blocks with CO2, water and sunlight

items.description:
Chinese researchers have developed a solar-powered method to convert carbon dioxide and water into chemicals that can serve as building blocks for petrol, mimicking the natural process of photosynthesis found in plants. The breakthrough could offer a more sustainable pathway to produce fuel for sectors that are difficult to electrify, such as aviation and shipping.

The team from the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology published their findings in the peer-reviewed journal Nature Communications last week. Drawing inspiration from how plants convert sunlight, CO2, and water into energy, the researchers created a specialized material that stores small amounts of electrical energy to efficiently drive chemical reactions.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: IAEA warns of nuclear risk after Russian strikes halt Ukraine plants

featured_image.name: IAEA chief warns of nuclear risk from Russia attacks on Ukraine power grids

items.description:
A massive Russian missile and drone attack struck Ukraine's energy infrastructure on February 7, forcing all nuclear power plants in Kyiv-controlled territory to halt electricity generation and prompting the International Atomic Energy Agency to issue urgent warnings about growing threats to nuclear safety.

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi called for military restraint after the strikes damaged key high-voltage substations that supply power to nuclear facilities, describing the deteriorating grid situation as compromising nuclear safety with potentially dangerous repercussions.[1][2][3]

items.title: SpaceX begins hiring for Musk's million-satellite data center plan

featured_image.name: SpaceX asks FCC to approve 1 million solar-powered AI data ...

items.description:
Elon Musk is moving forward with an audacious plan to build artificial intelligence data centers in space, with SpaceX now actively recruiting engineers for the project despite widespread skepticism from industry experts about its technical feasibility.

SpaceX filed an application with the Federal Communications Commission on January 30, 2026, seeking approval to launch up to one million satellites designed to operate as orbital data centers powered by near-constant solar energy. The company argues the system would "achieve transformative cost and energy efficiency while significantly reducing the environmental impact associated with terrestrial data centers."[1][2]
